observable_outcome: GET /v1/providers and a Providers section in the owner console report, for each of codex, claude and opencode: whether the owner's standing authorization covers it, whether the Loop has ever completed an invocation through it, a closed health value with its observation age and an explicit stale flag, a runaway-detection block that reports a stop for inspection by state and names the approved record the thresholds live in without copying the numbers, a concurrency block with the active assignment count and the ceiling with its source named, and the Executions currently assigned to it -- all derived only from observations the Loop's own execution path produced, with no CLI started, no probe, and a mechanical import scan proving there is no probe path.
acceptance_criteria: A1. Scope boundary, written before any code. The evidence opens with a table with one row per clause of cap-provider-operation's observable_result (connected or not; supported version and authentication health; concurrency limit, usage limit and exhaustion state; supported Loop Version; the Requirement currently assigned; handoff or waiting reason on failure or exhaustion) stating for each what this task makes observable, what it deliberately does not, and who owns the remainder. The row for 'supported version and Loop Version' must say plainly that this task does not introduce a version-compatibility check. The row for handoff must say that internal/provider.PrepareHandoff already exists and that wiring a handoff decision is not in this task. Nothing in the evidence may claim or imply that this task passes any release gate.

A2. Baseline, measured before changing anything. Record: the top-level test names and counts of internal/provider, internal/application, internal/api, internal/store/memory and internal/store/firestore and that all pass; the measured fact that the word provider appears in internal/api only in a comment in auth.go; and that no registry, health, limit or assignment surface exists in internal/api or internal/application. Every pre-existing test must still pass at the end under its existing name with its existing assertions unchanged, and the before/after top-level test counts per touched package must be reported.

A3. Provider identity as a closed set, pinned twice and independently. Add a test in internal/provider asserting that CodexAdapter.Name(), ClaudeAdapter.Name() and OpenCodeAdapter.Name() are exactly codex, claude, opencode and that no fourth adapter type exists in the package. Add a test in internal/application asserting the registry's own provider-name table is exactly that same three-element set in a documented order. internal/application must not import internal/provider; assert that by import scan (A11), not by inspection. Assert also that the openapi enum for the provider name is exactly those three values.

A4. Registry read model. internal/application gains ProviderRegistryView with one entry per declared Provider carrying: provider (closed enum), authorized (bool) and authorization_ref (string), verified_by_loop_invocation (bool), health (closed enum: unknown, healthy, degraded, unavailable, unauthenticated, stopped-for-inspection), blocked_reason (closed enum, empty when health is healthy), last_observed_at, observation_count, stale (bool), runaway_detection {scope, state in (within-thresholds, stopped-for-inspection, unknown), thresholds_declared_in}, concurrency {active_assignments, declared_ceiling, ceiling_source, remaining, exhausted}, and assignments (bounded list of {execution_id, increment_id, since}). Assert every enum is closed by a table test that fails if a constant is added without a case or a case without a constant. Assert the view is deterministic: the same stored state produces byte-identical JSON across repeated calls, with entries in a fixed order.

A5. Health is derived, never assumed, and silence is not health. Assert each of these directly, with an injected clock and no sleep: (a) a Provider with zero observations reports health unknown, stale true, observation_count 0, and blocked_reason never-invoked-by-loop, and never reports healthy; (b) one successful observation in the window reports healthy and verified_by_loop_invocation true; (c) a retryable failure class reports degraded; (d) a non-retryable failure class reports unavailable; (e) a provider-unauthenticated failure class reports health unauthenticated with blocked_reason owner-must-authenticate-cli-on-runner-machine; (f) an observation older than the declared window reports stale true with the previous health value preserved and reported as stale rather than silently refreshed; (g) the observation window is a named exported-or-documented constant and the number of observations retained per Provider is bounded by it, asserted by driving more observations than the bound and checking the retained count.

A6. A stop for inspection is neither success nor failure. When provider_observation.stopped_for_inspection is true, assert: health is stopped-for-inspection; runaway_detection.state is stopped-for-inspection; the Provider is not counted in any failure or degraded tally anywhere in the view; health is not unavailable; and the entry still reports its assignments and its concurrency block. Assert also that a stop for inspection does not make a later successful observation impossible to record, and that clearing it is not something this surface can do (the view has no mutation path for it).

A7. The naming requirement is enforced mechanically, not by review. Add a test that walks the marshalled JSON of a fully-populated ProviderRegistryView and the QueueSummary-independent openapi schema block added by this task, and fails if any object key or enum value contains any of the substrings budget, quota, billing, spend, cost, credit. Verify the matcher itself first against a known-positive (remaining_budget_usd) and a known-negative (runaway_detection) before trusting it. No numeric runaway threshold value may appear in the read model, the port, the stored record or the openapi schema; assert that too.

A8. Unauthenticated Providers are observable as the M6 wait. Build the measured present state as a fixture: standing authorization psa-foundation-001 covers codex, claude and opencode, and only claude has a completed Loop invocation. Assert the response reports authorized true for all three, verified_by_loop_invocation true for claude only, health unauthenticated or unknown with a named blocked_reason for codex and opencode, and that the two blocked entries are excluded from any assignable or eligible count the view reports. Assert that the approver value from contracts/schemas/provider-standing-authorization.json (an email address) appears nowhere in the response body, nowhere in the read model, and nowhere in any log line this task adds: scan the marshalled response bytes for an '@' inside the authorization fields as the positive control.

A9. Assignment. ProviderAssignmentRepository is a side table keyed by Execution id, written inside Start's existing transaction from the additive optional provider field on StartRequest. internal/domain is not touched: assert by git diff that no file under internal/domain changes. Assert: (a) starting an Execution with provider=claude makes that Execution appear in claude's assignments and in no other Provider's; (b) an Execution that reaches a terminal status is no longer reported as an active assignment; (c) starting without the field records no assignment and the Provider's active_assignments does not change; (d) an unknown provider value is rejected with 400 and records nothing; (e) the assignments list is bounded and the bound is asserted by exceeding it.

A10. No prompt, no response, no credential, structurally. provider_observation carries name, an optional closed failure_class enum and an optional boolean only. Assert there is no message, detail, output, result, session or text field on the request DTO, the port type, the stored record or the read model -- by AST field-name scan over the new types, so the guarantee is a property of the code and not of a redaction step. Assert a request body carrying an unknown field is rejected (additionalProperties:false plus the existing decoder), and that a failure_class value outside the closed enum is rejected with 400 and records nothing.

A11. There is no probe path, proven by import scan. Add internal/application/source_guard_test.go modelled on internal/domain/source_guard_test.go: parse every *.go file in internal/application with go/parser, fail outright on a zero-file scan, and assert no file imports os/exec, net, net/http, net/url, internal/provider or internal/runner. Verify the matcher against a known-positive and a known-negative path first. Record in the evidence that this is what makes docs/architecture/validation.md section 5's 'provider health probe does not grow with Requirement count' true at zero, and state the growth rate measured: number of provider CLI invocations caused by one GET /v1/providers is exactly zero, asserted by the scan plus the absence of any InvocationRunner or exec seam in the read path.

A12. Store adapters. Both internal/store/memory and internal/store/firestore implement the two new ports with bounded, keyed reads. For the Firestore adapter, record the measured read count for one GET /v1/providers against a fixture with the maximum bounded assignments and observations, and assert it is bounded by a constant that does not grow with Requirement count. Assert both adapters satisfy the same behavioural table (the same test table run against both) so the memory store cannot pass a behaviour the Firestore store does not implement. Do not change the quota reservation shape of any existing operation; assert that a GET /v1/providers read performs no write and no outbox record.

A13. API surface. GET /v1/providers requires the owner role: assert 401 without authentication, 403 for the runner role, 200 for the owner. Add the path and the response schema to contracts/openapi/openapi-v1.yaml with additionalProperties:false and every field in required, add the two additive optional request fields, and assert every existing openapi-conformance assertion in internal/contracts and internal/release still passes. Assert the response contains no synthetic or placeholder value and no field this Work Order did not name.

A14. Owner console. internal/web/owner.html gains a Providers section and owner.js renders the registry entries with health, blocked reason, staleness, the runaway-detection state and the assignment count. Do not render raw JSON for this section only to satisfy the item -- the reader must be able to see, without parsing, which Providers are waiting for owner authentication. Do not add any external asset, script or font: internal/web is embedded and must stay self-contained. Assert the rendered markup contains no credential-shaped and no email-shaped value.

A15. Documentation. Create docs/operations/provider-registry.md describing: the closed three-name identity and why it is name only; how health is derived and the explicit statement that nothing is probed and why probing would be caught by the runaway detector; the observation window and what stale means; the split between runaway_detection (runner-local, state only, thresholds in the named approved record) and concurrency (control-plane-owned); how an unauthenticated Provider appears and the exact human action required, stating that no agent can perform it; and one sentence recording the V2-062 boundary: the registry observes only the Loop's own execution path, so a Provider driven by hand outside the Loop is invisible to it and reports unknown. Do not edit any other document.

A16. Determinism. No fixed sleep, no wall-clock timer and no goroutine in any new test; every wait is a bounded deadline poll over an injected clock, and every timestamp comes from an injected clock. Run devbox run --pure -- go test -count=1 ./internal/application ./internal/api ./internal/provider three times in sequence and record that the verdict line and the output are identical each time, and run it once with -race.

A17. Measured notes for V2-045, recorded and not acted on. Record that ci/components.json declares application's dependencies as [domain] only while internal/application/ports.go already imports internal/quota (whose roots ci/components.json assigns to the infra component), and that this task adds no new import edge to application but does move the api, application, store-memory, store-firestore, provider, web, contracts and docs component keys. Record that editing contracts/openapi/openapi-v1.yaml moves the contracts key and is a declared contract dependency of the api and control-plane components. Only the application and api evidence records are issued here; name V2-045 as the owner of the remaining key movement under gate rule G6. Do not edit ci/components.json, Makefile, go.mod, go.sum or devbox.*; if a new component is genuinely required, stop and escalate to the tech_lead instead of editing.

A18. Evidence. Create .agents/v2/evidence/V2-067-application.json (id ev-v2-067-application, task_id V2-067, component application, correlation_id v2-067-provider-surface) and .agents/v2/evidence/V2-067-api.json (id ev-v2-067-api, task_id V2-067, component api, same correlation_id), recording for every check the argv actually executed, the working directory, the timeout and a summary stating the measured result, with every acceptance item above traceable to a named check. Record the execution environment identifier (uname -srm, go version, devbox environment). A skipped test is recorded with status skipped and is never counted as a pass (gate rule G7). No prompt, no raw provider response and no credential value in any form may appear in either record. Register both with exactly two appended entries in .agents/v2/evidence/index.json whose evidence_hash is the sha256 of each artifact's final committed bytes; touch no other task's entry. devbox run --pure -- go test -count=1 ./internal/contracts must be green with the records in place.

A19. Component evidence keys. The evidence_key recorded in each artifact is that component's key read with devbox run --pure -- make evidence-keys on the final tree where make check is green, with every touched file already git-added: a new file not in the index is invisible to that key.

A20. devbox run --pure -- make check is green, and it is re-run after the evidence commit so the secret scan reads committed history rather than an uncommitted tree. Record both runs and judge them by the verdict line, not by the shell exit status. No file outside allowed_paths changes.
constraints: Work only inside the assigned isolated task worktree; never push.
Never use git reset, git checkout --, git stash or git commit --amend.

Do not start a real Provider CLI (codex, claude or opencode) for any reason, including to determine whether it is authenticated. Health is derived from recorded observations and fixtures only. A probe would consume the runaway detector's own counters and is forbidden by dp-v2-067 d3.

Do not attempt to authenticate codex or opencode. Authentication uses the owner's identity and no agent may perform it; the unauthenticated state is the state this task must make observable, not a defect to fix.
Do not touch internal/domain. The existing transitions and the EffectFromPermit closure are not weakened, extended or bypassed; no domain file changes at all.

Do not touch ci/components.json, Makefile, go.mod, go.sum or devbox.*; the component dependency DAG and the toolchain surface are V2-045's task. If a new component is required, escalate instead of editing.
Do not weaken any capability declaration in contracts/release-contract/foundation-capabilities.json; that file is not edited by this task.

Do not edit .agents/v2/task-state/**, .agents/v2/packets/** or .agents/v2/provider-preflight/**; the coordinator records transitions and packets, and editing an approved preflight record breaks its approval digest binding by design.

Do not copy any numeric runaway threshold into the read model, the openapi schema or the owner console. Reaching a threshold is a stop for inspection, never a success and never a failure, and never a billing budget.

Do not record a prompt, a raw provider response, a session identifier or a credential value in any form -- not in a field, not in a log line, not in evidence. Do not carry the standing authorization's approver email into any response, read model or log.

Determinism is acceptance, not preference: no fixed sleep, no wall-clock timer, no goroutine in any new test. Waiting is bounded deadline polling over an injected clock, and a measured duration is logged as an observation, never asserted as a threshold.
A skipped test is never counted as a pass (gate rule G7). Record every skip explicitly with its status skipped and its reason, and record the execution environment identifier.
Never write a verification as passed that was not actually executed. If an acceptance item cannot be satisfied, stop and escalate to the tech_lead rather than fabricating or weakening it.
Every pre-existing test must keep passing under its existing name with its existing assertions unchanged. Report before and after top-level test counts per touched package.
Do not touch any Google Cloud resource; the Firestore assertions run against the local emulator path the existing store tests already use, or are recorded as skipped with their reason.

internal/scheduler, internal/runner, internal/reconciler and internal/release are read-only references here; do not edit them and do not import internal/provider or internal/runner from internal/application.
